The function being approximated, $S(t)$, is a staircase. Between zeros it falls with slope $-\Nsm'(t)\approx-1/\gap$, and at each zero it jumps up by 1. \begin{itemize}
\item At $\tau=0$, both sines vanish; their ratio tends to $(J+\frac12)\Delta\omega\tau/(\Delta\omega\tau/2)=2J+1$, so $K(0)=J=450$.

Containing approximately the right frequencies is not enough: the fit must also \emph{prefer} them. With more coefficients than data, infinitely many coefficient vectors fit the window exactly (Chapter~\ref{ch:least-squares}). patches.old: Aliasing. For samples equally spaced by $\Delta$, frequencies above $\pi/\Delta$ are indistinguishable from lower ones (Chapter~\ref{ch:fourier-transform}).
patches.new: Aliasing. Take samples equally spaced by $\Delta$, $t_n=n\Delta$. Two frequencies that differ by $2\pi/\Delta$ give identical samples: $e^{\ii(\omega+2\pi/\Delta)t_n}=e^{\ii\omega t_n}e^{2\pi\ii n}=e^{\ii\omega t_n}$, because $n$ is an integer. Also, $-\omega$ gives the same cosine samples as $\omega$ and sine samples of opposite sign, and the free sign of a fitted amplitude absorbs that. So every frequency has an alias in $[0,\pi/\Delta]$, and frequencies above $\pi/\Delta$ cannot be told apart from lower ones.

patches.new: \textbf{21.} As in the RE2 sample, the factor $m$ cancels on differentiation, so $F'(t)=-\frac{\log3}{\pi}\sum_{m=1}^3 3^{-m/2}\cos(mt\log3)$. Its maximum magnitude is $\frac{\log3}{\pi}(3^{-1/2}+3^{-1}+3^{-3/2})=0.3497\times1.1031=0.3858$, attained at $t=2\pi k/\log3$. Then $t^*=2\pi e^{2\pi\times0.3858}\approx70.9$. For the sum of the $p=2$ and $p=3$ waves the bound \eqref{eq:sparse-frequency-slope} is $0.3443+0.3858=0.7301$, giving $t^*=2\pi e^{2\pi\times0.7301}\approx617$. The holdout 401--500 lies at $t\ge680$, where $\Nsm'\ge0.745$. That exceeds both bounds, so a unique root is guaranteed in both cases, though only narrowly for the two-prime sum.

import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
dw = 8/450
j = np.arange(1, 451)
def D(tau):
    tau = np.asarray(tau, dtype=float)
    out = np.empty_like(tau)
    for i in range(0, tau.size, 2000):
        out[i:i+2000] = np.cos(np.outer(tau[i:i+2000], j*dw)).sum(axis=1)
    return out
Trep = 2*np.pi/dw
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(6.5, 3))
ta = np.linspace(-2, 2, 2001)
ax[0].plot(ta, D(ta), lw=0.8)
ax[0].axhline(0, color="0.7", lw=0.5)
ax[0].set_xlabel(r"$\tau$ (height difference, dimensionless)")
ax[0].set_ylabel(r"$D(\tau)$")
